title: RB1 Runtime Architecture T0-T7 Applicability and State-Transition Authority

scope.rule: Resolve only architecture applicability and state/execution semantics. No physical science, production/reference change, numerical-policy change or whole-capability maturity promotion may be inferred.

applicability_policy.T0_T1: NOT_APPLICABLE for pure runtime topology/state semantics where no physical phenomenon or scientific theory is introduced; process science remains inherited.
applicability_policy.T2_T3: May be RESOLVED as controlled conceptual, ownership and state-transition semantics even when no physical-process model is introduced.
applicability_policy.T4_T5: NOT_APPLICABLE where runtime composition selects or changes no physical formulation.
applicability_policy.T6: Applicable to interval partitioning, batching, worker partitioning or committed split-run boundaries; runtime scheduling is not thereby reclassified as physical discretisation.
applicability_policy.T7: Applicable only where the capability itself defines numerical acceptance/solver semantics. Scheduling, worker-count admission and persistence are not silently promoted into numerical-method authority.

T0.rationale: Interval orchestration is not a physical phenomenon.

T2.rationale: No independent physical conceptual model is introduced.

T3.rationale: No independent physical equation system is defined.

T4.rationale: No physical parameterisation belongs to interval orchestration.

T5.rationale: No independent continuous physical formulation belongs to interval orchestration.

T6.meaning: Generic [t0,t1] partition into accepted committed substeps.

T7.rationale: Acceptance/retry numerical policy belongs to transaction/temporal capabilities.

T0.rationale: N=1 is execution cardinality, not a physical phenomenon.

T1.rationale: N=1 introduces no scientific theory; process theory is inherited.

T2.meaning: One logical column uses the same serialized physical MultiSWAP composition as N>1; there is no separate standalone kernel.

T3.meaning: Cardinality changes only logical-column count; explicit template, parameter, forcing and committed-state identities remain unchanged.

T5.rationale: N=1 introduces no continuous physical formulation.

T6.meaning: Execution covers caller-supplied [t0,t1] and deterministic batching may contain one logical column without calendar-boundary semantics.

T7.rationale: N=1 introduces no independent numerical solver/acceptance method.

capabilities.nonclaim: No separate standalone kernel or legacy file-I/O release API is inferred.

T0.rationale: Serial MultiSWAP is runtime composition, not a physical phenomenon.

T1.rationale: Serial MultiSWAP introduces no independent scientific theory.

T2.meaning: Logical columns reference template, immutable parameter, forcing and committed-state identities while sharing the serialized physical route.

T3.meaning: Explicit column/template/state identity, deterministic execution order and non-aliased authoritative state define isolation/equivalence semantics.

T4.rationale: Serial composition changes no physical parameterisation.

T5.rationale: Serial composition changes no continuous physical formulation.

T6.meaning: The ordered column set is partitioned into deterministic batches over one caller-supplied [t0,t1].

T7.rationale: Serial MultiSWAP defines no new solver/acceptance method; kernel numerical policy is inherited.

capabilities.nonclaim: No whole-domain performance or speedup claim is introduced.

T0.rationale: Parallel scheduling is runtime execution, not a physical phenomenon.

T1.rationale: Parallel scheduling introduces no scientific theory.

T2.meaning: Logical columns remain independently identified; worker-owned backends/transaction controls provide worker-local execution context while immutable/template identities are shared references.

T3.meaning: Unique column/state ownership, deterministic assignment/publication and equivalence to the admitted serialized column route are required invariants.

T4.rationale: Parallel scheduling changes no physical parameterisation.

T5.rationale: Parallel scheduling changes no continuous physical formulation.

T6.meaning: RB1 deterministically partitions admitted columns across exactly 2 or 4 workers with batch barriers and canonical publication over the same [t0,t1].

T7.rationale: Worker-count admission/scheduling is runtime policy, not a replacement numerical solver or acceptance method.

capabilities.nonclaim: No speedup, throughput superiority or unsupported-worker-count claim is introduced.

T0.rationale: Restart is persistence/runtime semantics, not a physical phenomenon.

T1.rationale: Restart semantics introduce no scientific theory.

T2.meaning: Continuation contains compact committed physical state plus stable runtime/template/parameter identity; immutable parameters, forcing and solver scratch are excluded.

T3.meaning: Committed readiness, schema/template/parameter identity, state-family sufficiency and atomic all-record restore are required invariants; failed restore publishes no partial target state.

T4.rationale: Restart persistence changes no physical parameterisation.

T5.rationale: Restart persistence changes no continuous physical formulation.

T6.meaning: A split-run boundary is a committed model-time boundary carried by persisted state, independent of midnight/day boundaries.

T7.rationale: Persistence defines no post-restore numerical solver; continuation equivalence is a verification/qualification obligation.

capabilities.nonclaim: No filesystem format, cross-version migration, mid-transaction restart or solver/Newton/Jacobian/warm-start persistence is claimed.

T0.rationale: Parallel restart is runtime continuation semantics, not a physical phenomenon.

T1.rationale: Parallel restart introduces no scientific theory.

T2.meaning: Restart state is per logical column and independent of worker identity; worker-local scratch is excluded so committed continuation can be rebound to an admitted worker topology.

T3.meaning: Column/template/parameter/state-family identity and atomic restore are preserved; worker repartition must not alter restored committed physical state.

T4.rationale: Parallel restart changes no physical parameterisation.

T5.rationale: Parallel restart changes no continuous physical formulation.

T6.meaning: Committed split-run boundaries are worker-count independent; RB1 qualification includes admitted 2-to-4 and 4-to-2 continuation.

T7.rationale: Worker repartition is runtime policy, not a numerical solver method; deterministic equivalence belongs to verification/qualification.

capabilities.nonclaim: No mid-transaction restart, trial-state persistence or worker/Newton/Jacobian/warm-start persistence is claimed.
